result.summary: The image shows a high-speed, multi-lane divided roadway with no visible pedestrian infrastructure. The complete absence of sidewalks and marked crossings makes this environment extremely hostile and dangerous for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Absence of sidewalks
hazards.description: There are no paved walkways, forcing pedestrians to walk on the grass or the road shoulder near high-speed traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the foreground and background roadways.

hazards.name: Lack of protected crossing
hazards.description: The multi-lane divided road has no marked crosswalks or signals, requiring pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic unprotected.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire visible roadway width.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous paved sidewalks on both sides of the roadway to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk and Pedestrian Signal
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian-activated signal (like an RRFB or HAWK) to provide a safe crossing point.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with a sidewalk but a complete lack of formal pedestrian crossing infrastructure at the intersection. While mature trees provide a buffer and shade, the absence of marked crosswalks, curb ramps, and clear sightlines at the corner creates a challenging environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to indicate a pedestrian crossing at the intersection.

hazards.name: Missing Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The sidewalk ends at a vertical curb without a ramp, creating an accessibility barrier.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk on the right

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Large trees and bushes at the corner may block the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection corner

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at the intersection corners.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential intersection featuring a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps and street lighting is present, the crossing lacks active traffic control or daylighting to ensure pedestrian visibility and safety.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb near the crosswalk may block the sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, approaching the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks a stop sign or signal, requiring pedestrians to rely on drivers yielding voluntarily.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground at the zebra markings.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and prevent illegal parking near the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Enhanced Signage
interventions.description: Install pedestrian crossing warning signs or a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB) to increase driver awareness.

result.summary: The image depicts a multi-lane arterial road designed primarily for high-speed vehicular traffic, lacking any visible pedestrian infrastructure such as sidewalks or marked crossings. The environment is hostile to pedestrians due to the wide roadway, lack of separation from traffic, and absence of safe crossing points.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalks
hazards.description: There are no paved walkways for pedestrians, forcing anyone on foot to walk in the grass or on the roadway shoulder.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway throughout the visible area.

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: The wide, multi-lane configuration encourages high vehicle speeds and creates a long, unprotected crossing distance.

interventions.title: Install Sidewalks
interventions.description: Construct paved sidewalks on both sides of the road to provide a dedicated and safe space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Road Diet and Lane Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the number of travel lanes or narrow existing lanes to lower vehicle speeds and shorten crossing distances.

interventions.title: Marked Pedestrian Crossings
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks, potentially with pedestrian-actuated signals or RRFBs, to facilitate safe crossing.
